==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=MassTransit&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Plugins/MassTransitTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=MassTransit&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using MassTransit;
using MassTransit.Testing;

// Verify.MassTransit: Snapshots a MassTransit test harness: the messages sent, published and consumed, and saga state changes.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.MassTransit
// Note: Guids are scrubbed to Guid_N by Verify core, so InVar.Id and the correlation ids stay
// stable between runs.
// Note: The harness has to be started and stopped around the test; the finally keeps a failure
// from leaving it running.
// Note: Everything is in memory: no broker, container or transport is needed.
public class MassTransitTests
{
    // Verifying the harness and the consumer harness together replaces a run of asserts: the
    // snapshot lists what was sent, what was published in response, and what was consumed.
    // The harness is in memory, so no broker is involved.
    [Fact]
    public async Task ConsumerHarness()
    {
        using var harness = new InMemoryTestHarness();
        var consumer = harness.Consumer<SubmitOrderConsumer>();

        await harness.Start();
        try
        {
            await harness.InputQueueSendEndpoint
                .Send(
                    new SubmitOrder
                    {
                        OrderId = InVar.Id
                    });

            await Verify(
                new
                {
                    harness,
                    consumer
                });
        }
        finally
        {
            await harness.Stop();
        }
    }

    // A saga harness adds the saga instances and their state changes to the snapshot, so a
    // state machine is covered by one verified file instead of an assert per transition.
    [Fact]
    public async Task SagaHarness()
    {
        using var harness = new InMemoryTestHarness();
        var sagaHarness = harness.Saga<ConsumerSaga>();

        var correlationId = NewId.NextGuid();

        await harness.Start();
        try
        {
            await harness.Bus.Publish(
                new Start
                {
                    CorrelationId = correlationId
                });

            await harness.Consumed.Any<Start>();

            await Verify(
                new
                {
                    harness,
                    sagaHarness
                });
        }
        finally
        {
            await harness.Stop();
        }
    }
}
